generic-link-text-no-rescuing-context: A link reads only 'click here' or 'read more' (or a raw URL) with no nearby explaining text, so a screen-reader user listing links can't tell where any goes.
context-outside-programmatic-link-contex: The text explaining a vague link exists on the page but sits in a separate paragraph or cell, so a screen reader never connects it to the link.
icon-link-name-present-but-wrong-or-mean: An icon-only link has a label, but it misdescribes the icon or is useless (a search icon labeled 'image'), so screen-reader users are misled about it.
duplicate-name-same-context-different-pu: Several links share the same text and surroundings yet lead to genuinely different places, so a user picking from them can't tell which one does what they want.
preceding-heading-or-list-grouping-conte: A vague link like 'Map' or 'Book now' only makes sense from the heading above it, raising whether that heading is really tied to the link well enough.
descriptive-name-contradicts-on-page-des: A link has a clear, specific label that is wrong about its target (a 'Privacy Policy' link jumping to the Terms section), deceiving users about where it goes.
